quote: No source specifies whether the soy sauce or other seasonings used in savory dishes (such as the taco rice or curries) are wheat-free. Most Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so celiac diners should confirm directly before ordering savory items.
found: UNCITED in the record. Went looking: the cafe's own Arashiyama page publishes the full savory menu (chickpea-and-tomato curry set, spaghetti set, veg taco rice set, miso soup, house pickles, three-part-polished rice) with no seasoning, soy-sauce or allergen information of any kind - which is exactly what the claim asserts.
note: Repairable rather than deletable: cite musubi-cafe.jp/arashiyama as the page that publishes the savory menu without any seasoning detail. Note the same page shows a spaghetti set, i.e. wheat pasta in this kitchen.

quote: The menu is reported to be clearly labeled, making it easy to see which items are vegan, and staff are said to understand what vegan cooking ("vegan ryori") means.
found: Venue blurb: 'There is an English menu, and the staff understand what "vegan ryori" is.' Reviewer: 'We didn't have lunch but the menu is well labeled and easy to see what is vegan or not.'
note: Both halves verbatim, including the 'vegan ryori' phrase.

quote: Daily blackboard specials follow a pattern where one option is always vegan-friendly.
found: 'The blackboard shows two additional choices for that day's lunch. Option A is always vegan-friendly and option B is a meat option.'
note: Verbatim - but read the second half of that sentence: option B is MEAT. See the vegan_status flag on this record.

quote: Staff are repeatedly described as exceptionally friendly and accommodating, including preparing a vegan set that had sold out for one guest.
found: 'Since it was already later in the day they were apparently sold out on their vegan lunch set but the women were so incredibly friendly and still prepared it for me' - plus many other 'Friendly staff' Pros lines.
note: Verbatim. Note this is hospitality, not an allergen protocol - the field name overpromises slightly.

quote: The cafe's sister dessert operation was built specifically around egg, dairy, and wheat allergies, indicating allergy awareness is central to the business, though no formal cross-contamination protocol is documented.
found: Home page, sweets-factory panel: 「卵、乳、小麦粉アレルギーのお子さまへ。友達と、家族と一緒にケーキを囲んで欲しい。」 (To children with egg, dairy and wheat-flour allergies - we want you to be able to gather around a cake with friends and family.) Also 「アレルギーの方のみならずアスリートにもグルテンフリー食生活を送る方が増えてきている」.
note: Supported, and the 'no formal CC protocol documented' hedge is accurate - the site publishes none.

quote: All desserts are 100% vegan and gluten-free, with nine such desserts available, and the dessert program was created expressly so people with egg, dairy, and wheat allergies can enjoy cake.
found: /sweets-factory: 「スイーツは植物性食材のみ使用、米粉やナッツパウダーなど、小麦粉を使用しないグルテンフリー仕様です。」 Home page: 「卵、乳、小麦粉アレルギーのお子さまへ。友達と、家族と一緒にケーキを囲んで欲しい。」
note: CAUTION for celiacs. The count 'nine' is not on musubi-cafe.jp - it is thejapaneserose's ('With nine vegan and gluten-free desserts'); the site lists 8 sweets at the factory and 7 at the cafe. And the blanket 'all desserts' overstates the cafe branch: on musubi-cafe.jp/arashiyama the cakes that are wheat-free say so explicitly (「米粉を使い、小麦粉不使用」) while the plain パウンドケーキ 500 says only 「バター・卵・生クリームなどの動物性食品不使用」. Scope the claim to musubi sweets factory.

quote: Vegan options are clearly marked and easy to identify on the menu, and staff understand vegan cooking.
found: 'the menu is well labeled and easy to see what is vegan or not' and 'There is an English menu, and the staff understand what "vegan ryori" is.'

quote: The cafe emphasizes locally sourced ingredients and food that is gentle on body and mind, with vegan curry, taco rice, and pasta available.

quote: This is a conveyor-belt (kaiten-zushi) restaurant, so plates of many different items pass continuously over your seat. That open belt creates real potential for cross-contact, so it is best treated as manageable for non-celiac gluten-avoiders rather than celiac-safe.
found: Page title 'Kura Zushi Purasu-gata tenpo kyoto teramachidoori - Kyoto Kawaramachi/Kaiten sushi (Conveyor belt sushi)'; category line 'Kyoto Kawaramachi Sta./Kaiten sushi (Conveyor belt sushi), Sushi'.
note: Tabelog confirms the kaiten format and nothing else - it says nothing about cross-contact, and the risk reasoning is the record's. 'Open belt' is factually wrong for Kura: every plate travels under the domed 'Sendo-kun' lid, described in the Taipei Times article this same record cites ('a transparent dome-shaped cover placed on top of each plate of sushi'). Keep the celiac caution, fix the mechanism.

quote: An allergen and ingredient chart is available in English on the Kura Sushi website; roughly a quarter of menu items are free of wheat, so a careful diner can build a meal, but should verify each item on the chart.
found: The English site's footer links 'Allergen' -> https://www.kurasushi.co.jp/trans/common/pdf/kura_allergen_en.pdf and 'Ingredients'. The PDF is a 5-page 'Kurasushi allergen and calorie information' chart, 'As of August 12, 2026', with a Wheat column.
method: plain fetch, iPhone UA; PDF fetched and text-extracted with pdftotext
note: Chart existence verified. The quantitative 'roughly a quarter of menu items are free of wheat' is NOT verifiable as written - the PDF is a symbol matrix and no count is published; either recompute it from the PDF or drop the fraction. Also carry the PDF's own caveat: 'Large volumes of items are handled at our processing centers and restaurants, so an ingredient may unintentionally get mixed in with or get attached to another ... it is not an assurance of condition on serving.'

quote: Kura makes its own soy sauce in-house as part of its no-additives policy, but this does not make it gluten-free, standard Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat. Assume the house soy sauce contains wheat and bring your own tamari or certified gluten-free soy sauce.
found: 'In a typical sushi restaurant, those would be in the vinegar for the sushi rice and the soy sauce and wasabi mustard used to flavor the sushi, but in Kura's restaurants, they're all custom-made to avoid this, according to Tanaka.'
note: Supported that the soy sauce is custom-made to be additive-free. The article says nothing about wheat, so the 'assume it contains wheat' advice is the record's own inference - sound, but should not read as sourced. 'Makes its own soy sauce in-house' is also stronger than 'custom-made'.

quote: Some plant-forward plates exist (for example avocado-based rolls), but on a shared conveyor belt that carries fish and seafood, incidental cross-contact is likely; strict vegans should confirm preparation with staff.
found: The only avocado item anywhere on the cited Tabelog page is a reviewer's line item 'Salmon Avocado Cheese JPY 150' - salmon and cheese, not a plant-forward plate. The page describes no vegan or plant-based options and says nothing about cross-contact.
note: The cited page does not support any part of this claim, and its one avocado item actively undercuts the example given. Matches the 'vegan claim on a page serving salmon' defect shape. Re-source from the Kura allergen chart or drop the avocado example.

quote: Kura publishes a detailed allergen and ingredient chart in English on its website, which makes it easier than at most casual sushi spots to identify which items are free of wheat and other allergens.
